tiers.1: Highest fit — large reach, proven digital literacy interest, likely budget
tiers.2: Strong fit — good reach, may need warm introduction
tiers.3: Emerging fit — smaller reach or less proven interest, longer sales cycle

prospects.name: London Public Library
prospects.notes: Large urban system, strong digital literacy programming history. Has run seniors tech workshops. 16 branches. High priority.

prospects.name: St. Thomas Public Library
prospects.notes: Home community — highest personal connection. Ideal for pilot partnership. Aaron should visit in person first.

prospects.name: Elgin County Library
prospects.notes: County library system serving rural Elgin — 8 branches. Strong seniors programming. Ready — pending Aaron approval before send.

prospects.name: Aylmer & East Elgin Community Complex
prospects.notes: Small community hub with library and programming space. Good pilot site for rural deployment. Ready — pending Aaron approval before send.

prospects.name: Woodstock Public Library
prospects.notes: Mid-size community library, active senior programming. Oxford County has high senior population proportion.

prospects.name: Stratford Public Library
prospects.notes: Arts-focused community, engaged civic participation. Testimonial from Robert in Stratford already on site.

prospects.name: Owen Sound Public Library
prospects.notes: Grey-Bruce region has above-average senior demographic. Rural-adjacent — digital access challenges well understood here.

prospects.name: Sarnia Public Library
prospects.notes: Active digital programs for seniors. Lambton County has strong industrial heritage — many retired workers in demographic.

prospects.name: Chatham-Kent Public Library
prospects.notes: Multi-branch system across a large rural-urban municipality. Strong community services mandate. Good fit for regional rollout.

prospects.name: Tillsonburg Public Library
prospects.notes: Small community but very high senior proportion. Word-of-mouth potential. Low-cost entry point for regional expansion.

prospects.name: Simcoe Public Library
prospects.notes: Norfolk County library system. Agricultural community, high senior demographic, limited digital literacy programming.

prospects.name: Norfolk County Public Library
prospects.notes: Multi-branch rural system. Very high need for digital literacy programming. Budget may be tight — explore grant-funded partnership.

prospects.name: Libro Credit Union
prospects.notes: Largest credit union in SW Ontario. Strong community investment programme. Has funded digital inclusion initiatives before. Top priority.

prospects.name: Meridian Credit Union
prospects.notes: Ontario's largest credit union. Has major community investment arm. B2B proposal should emphasise fraud protection for members — strong business case.

prospects.name: FirstOntario Credit Union
prospects.notes: Large credit union with strong senior member base. Active member education programmes. Good fit for Module 6 (Banking) co-branding.

prospects.name: Libro Credit Union (Elgin Branch)
prospects.notes: Local Libro branch — ideal for pilot with Aaron's home community connection. Approach branch manager directly before corporate.

prospects.name: Entegra Credit Union
prospects.notes: Out-of-province — noted for future expansion to western Canada. Low priority for now.

prospects.name: Kawartha Credit Union
prospects.notes: Mid-size CU with strong community roots. Kawartha Lakes region has high senior population. Active financial literacy programming.

prospects.name: Northern Credit Union
prospects.notes: Northern Ontario — underserved digital literacy market. Many branch closures in region driving digital banking adoption among seniors.

prospects.name: PACE Credit Union
prospects.notes: Public sector employee focus. Urban Toronto market. Good fit for pilot with municipal employees who support seniors.

prospects.name: Alterna Savings
prospects.notes: Strong bilingual capacity — French/English — aligns with DCC bilingual commitment. Good fit for Ottawa francophone seniors.

prospects.name: Innovation Credit Union
prospects.notes: Out-of-province. Noted for future Prairie expansion. Low priority for Ontario-first rollout.

prospects.name: United Way Elgin Middlesex
prospects.notes: Covers Aaron's home region. Strong track record funding digital inclusion. DCC aligns directly with their senior poverty-reduction mandate.

prospects.name: Age-Friendly London
prospects.notes: City of London initiative. WHO Age-Friendly City designation holder. Direct connection to senior services. Ideal institutional partner.

prospects.name: Elgin County
prospects.notes: County government — potential to fund programme through Seniors Services budget. Aaron's local government connection.

prospects.name: City of St. Thomas
prospects.notes: Home city government. High level of interest possible through Mayor's office. Seniors Services budget applicable.

prospects.name: VON Canada SW Ontario
prospects.notes: Victorian Order of Nurses — visits isolated seniors at home. DCC could be distributed through their care workers. Excellent channel partner.

prospects.name: CMHA Thames Valley
prospects.notes: Mental health focus — digital isolation link is strong argument. DCC helps reduce isolation which CMHA cares about deeply.

prospects.name: Alzheimer Society SW Ontario
prospects.notes: Strong case for Module 1 (Escape Hatch) as confusion-reduction for early-stage dementia. Could position DCC as part of cognitive support toolkit.

prospects.name: Victorian Order of Nurses
prospects.notes: National reach. If VON adopts DCC as a programme tool, deployment across Canada is possible. Longer sales cycle but transformative.

prospects.name: Community Living London
prospects.notes: Primarily serves people with developmental disabilities, not seniors specifically. Some overlap in accessible design mission. Lower priority.

prospects.name: Parkwood Institute
prospects.notes: St. Joseph's Health Care London — Parkwood specialises in geriatric and rehab care. DCC as part of discharge planning / patient education toolkit is compelling.
